criteria.name: Empathy and Patient-Centred Tone
criteria.description: Assesses whether the provider acknowledges the patient's feelings, concerns, and lived experience with warmth and respect.

levels.label: Absent
levels.description: Dismissive of patient concerns; focuses solely on clinical data without acknowledging the patient as a person.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: Acknowledges some concerns but empathy is inconsistent or feels formulaic.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Consistently acknowledges the patient's emotional state and concerns; normalises experiences and validates feelings throughout.

criteria.name: Plain Language and Jargon Avoidance
criteria.description: Evaluates whether the provider explains diagnoses, procedures, and instructions in language the patient can understand, avoiding unexplained medical jargon.

levels.label: Heavy Jargon
levels.description: Uses multiple unexplained medical terms; patient is likely to leave confused.

levels.label: Mostly Clear
levels.description: Generally clear but includes some unexplained terms or overly complex phrasing.

levels.label: Fully Accessible
levels.description: Consistently uses everyday language; explains any necessary medical terms with simple analogies or examples.

criteria.name: Active Listening
criteria.description: Measures whether the provider allows the patient to finish speaking, reflects back what they heard, and responds to the actual concern raised rather than a generic assumption.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Interrupts frequently or ignores key patient statements; responses feel disconnected from what the patient said.

levels.label: Adequate
levels.description: Listens in most exchanges but occasionally talks over the patient or misses an explicit concern.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Consistently lets the patient finish; reflects back concerns accurately; probes for more when needed.

criteria.name: Shared Decision-Making
criteria.description: Assesses whether the provider explains options, invites the patient's preference, and ensures decisions are made collaboratively rather than prescribed unilaterally.

levels.label: Absent
levels.description: Provider dictates the plan with no invitation for patient input or questions.

levels.label: Token
levels.description: Offers a brief opportunity for questions but does not genuinely explore patient preferences or concerns about options.

levels.label: Collaborative
levels.description: Explains options with pros and cons in plain terms; elicits the patient's priorities and incorporates them into the plan.

criteria.name: Clarity of Next Steps
criteria.description: Evaluates how clearly the provider explains what the patient should do after the visit, including medications, activity, and when to seek further care.

levels.label: Unclear
levels.description: Next steps are vague, missing, or contradictory; patient is likely unsure what to do.

levels.label: Mostly Clear
levels.description: Key next steps are covered but timeline or conditions for seeking urgent care are missing.

levels.label: Fully Clear
levels.description: Next steps are specific, sequenced, and include when to return, what to watch for, and how to reach the team if needed.

criteria.name: Patient Education
criteria.description: Assesses whether the provider proactively explains the patient's condition and recovery in a way that builds understanding and self-management confidence.

levels.label: None
levels.description: No educational content provided; patient leaves without understanding their condition or recovery.

levels.label: Basic
levels.description: Some explanation given but gaps remain; patient may not understand why they are doing what is recommended.

levels.label: Thorough
levels.description: Explains the 'why' behind recommendations; uses relatable examples; checks understanding and invites follow-up questions.

criteria.name: Checking for Understanding
criteria.description: Measures whether the provider verifies that the patient understood the key information before concluding the visit.

levels.label: Absent
levels.description: No check for understanding; visit ends abruptly without confirming patient comprehension.

levels.label: Minimal
levels.description: Asks once (e.g. 'Any questions?') but does not probe whether the patient genuinely understood.

levels.label: Thorough
levels.description: Uses teach-back or targeted questions to confirm understanding; addresses any remaining gaps before closing.

criteria.name: Pronunciation and Pacing
criteria.description: Evaluates whether the provider speaks clearly, at an appropriate pace, with good diction — particularly important when speaking with patients for whom English is not a first language.

levels.label: Difficult to Follow
levels.description: Speaks too fast, mumbles, or has significant pronunciation issues that impede comprehension.

levels.label: Generally Clear
levels.description: Mostly clear but occasionally rushes through complex instructions or important information.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Speaks at a calm, patient-appropriate pace; enunciates clearly; pauses naturally to allow patient processing.
